programs.name: verhulst
programs.purpose: Solve the Verhulst logistic population growth equation and output the sampled results as binary floats.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: VERHULST - solve the VERHULST logistic equation

params.name: stepmax
params.description: Number of output samples and solver advances.

params.name: mode
params.description: Output x, y, z, xy, xz, or yz components. The selfdoc also lists xyz, but the parser rejects it.

params.name: toutfile
params.description: If nonempty, write output times as binary floats to this file.

params.name: verbose
params.description: If nonzero, report solver step counts and error tolerance.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The adaptive Runge-Kutta-England solver uses iterative double-precision calculations and converts output to float. Its derivative callback mutates y[1] even though the solver is initialized for one equation; the reported y component reflects callback side effects rather than a separately integrated variable. The z component remains zero. Solver step acceptance and floating-point evaluation order can affect results.
programs.difficulty_reason: Porting requires reproducing an adaptive iterative ODE solver and the callback's state mutation.

test_cases.description: Sample population with explicitly chosen initial conditions and time step.
test_cases.command: verhulst stepmax=32 mode=x y0=10 a1=1.0 a2=2000 h=0.01 tol=1e-8 > population.bin

test_cases.description: Output population and callback-derived growth rate, plus sample times.
test_cases.command: verhulst stepmax=24 mode=xy y0=20 a1=0.8 a2=500 h=0.05 tol=1e-7 toutfile=times.bin > population_rate.bin

test_cases.description: Exercise the zero-valued z component in paired output.
test_cases.command: verhulst stepmax=16 mode=yz y0=5 a1=0.5 a2=100 h=0.1 > rate_zero.bin

programs.name: voltlotka
programs.purpose: Solve a predator-prey population model with a prey carrying capacity and output the sampled populations as binary floats.

params.name: b
params.description: Prey reduction rate due to predation.

params.name: d
params.description: Documented as the predator increase coefficient, but never read by the code; use p instead.

params.name: p
params.description: Predator increase coefficient; the selfdoc calls this parameter d.

params.name: thresh
params.description: The derivative callback sets either population to zero when it is at or below this threshold.

params.name: stepmax
params.description: Number of output samples and solver advances.

params.name: mode
params.description: PP outputs all prey samples followed by all predator samples; R outputs prey only and Y outputs predator only. The selfdoc reverses these component labels.

params.name: verbose
params.description: If nonzero, report solver step counts and error tolerance.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The adaptive Runge-Kutta-England solver uses iterative double-precision calculations and converts output to float; threshold comparisons and callback mutation of the populations affect subsequent solver steps. The code initializes the solver for three equations but supplies a two-element state array and initializes only two derivative components, causing out-of-bounds access and use of an uninitialized derivative. Results therefore rely on undefined behavior and may vary by platform or build.
programs.difficulty_reason: Porting requires an adaptive iterative ODE solver and a decision about the original program's undefined behavior.

test_cases.description: Output both population series with explicit model parameters.
test_cases.command: voltlotka stepmax=32 mode=PP x0=500 y0=25 a=0.5 b=0.02 c=0.75 p=0.005 K=1000000 h=0.1 tol=1e-8 thresh=1 > populations.bin

test_cases.description: Output the prey series with a smaller carrying capacity.
test_cases.command: voltlotka stepmax=24 mode=R x0=100 y0=10 a=0.4 b=0.01 c=0.6 p=0.004 K=1000 h=0.05 > prey.bin

test_cases.description: Exercise the extinction threshold and predator-only output.
test_cases.command: voltlotka stepmax=16 mode=Y x0=2 y0=0.5 thresh=1 h=0.1 > predator.bin
